clue.text: Father, for example, welcomes post being returned to the house

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the father figure holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a father is one kind of parent

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for post is read from the end to the start

parts.note: post is mail

explanation.surface: A dad, letters in hand, sends the post back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The house' is the legislature, as in Britain's House of Commons, not a home; 'being returned' turns the post word round before 'welcomes' takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament sits as a house, as in the Houses of Commons and Lords, so the legislative chamber is the house.

clue.text: Answer found in favourite fuel

indicators.note: one piece is discovered sitting inside the other

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A reply discovered in somebody's preferred kind of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried peat is cut from bogs and burned as a fuel in Ireland and Scotland.

clue.text: Ceremony that's correct for the listeners

indicators.note: what an audience hears, so the word is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: correct means right

explanation.surface: A ceremony that is proper for those listening in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a ritual or formal religious ceremony.

clue.text: One unable to speak about quiet attribute

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: around, so the word for unable to speak goes round the quiet letter

parts.note: unable to speak means mute
P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot talk, quietly attributing blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute a fault is to ascribe or assign it to someone, a verb sense of attribute.

clue.text: Average white band on the way?

explanation.surface: An ordinary line painted down a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: the white line painted down the centre of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road means moderate or unremarkable, and literally names the centre line marking a street.

clue.text: Want to take a run, and got close

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside

parts.note: to want is to need
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Wanting to go for a run and getting near.
explanation.definitionFit: Neared is the past tense of near, meaning approached or drew closer.

clue.text: Set fund taking the odds for stallion

indicators.note: keep only the letters in odd positions of these words: first, third, fifth, seventh

explanation.surface: A fund established, betting on the odds for a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a male horse kept for breeding, a stallion.

clue.text: News presenters broadcast rector's win

indicators.note: scattered widely, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the s included

explanation.surface: Newsreaders announcing that a clergyman has won.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s of rector's is used as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Town criers once announced the news in public squares, so they were presenters of news before broadcasting.

clue.text: Cleans up cid fitness to operate

indicators.note: set to work, so these letters are worked into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Detectives keeping fit before they can get on with the job.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinfects means sterilises, clearing away germs from a surface.

clue.text: One paid out to chase worker from the south

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the worker

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

indicators.note: out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who was paid off hunting down an employee from down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' is the definition: Antipodean means of Australia or New Zealand, seen from Britain; 'out' rearranges the letters and 'to chase' puts them after the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean describes Australia and New Zealand, lands in the far southern hemisphere.

clue.text: Cries of pain over lake birds

indicators.note: the cries sit over and around the lake, so it is held inside them

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain, so ows are several

explanation.surface: Birds hooting in distress across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are nocturnal birds of prey.

clue.text: Finishes welcoming visit, and escapes

indicators.note: taking a guest in, so the finishing word holds the visit inside

parts.note: finishes means closes
to call is to pay a visit

explanation.surface: Ending a social visit, then getting away.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call is a narrow escape from disaster.

clue.text: Dropping unconscious, and breaking ranks

parts.note: dropping means falling
knocked out means unconscious

explanation.surface: Collapsing senseless, a soldier leaves the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers fall out when they leave their ranks; it also means quarrelling and splitting from others.

clue.text: Said something after son followed

indicators.note: the speaking word is placed after the abbreviation for son

parts.note: to say something is to talk

explanation.surface: A father speaking after his son has spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To stalk is to follow someone stealthily or persistently.

clue.text: Close look at sleep?

parts.note: to close is to shut
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Peering closely at someone sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is informal for a nap or rest.

clue.text: Free of French meat

parts.note: de is French for of
liver is offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: Offal served without French influence.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to rescue or set them free, as in deliver us from evil.

clue.text: There's nothing in turner to dislike

indicators.note: sits inside, so the zero goes within the turning machine

parts.note: a lathe turns wood or metal while it is cut
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A painter like Turner has nothing to hate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turner' looks like the painter J. M. W. Turner, but here it is a machine that turns things.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to hate intensely, a strong form of disliking.

clue.text: A swindle by outwardly divine man of the church

indicators.note: only the outside of the word is kept: its first and last letters

parts.note: a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A con trick committed by a holy man who only looks pious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' gives the first and last letters of divine, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranked below a priest.

clue.text: To separately live is such

parts.note: the phrase itself pushes an adverb between to and its verb, the grammatical fault it names

explanation.surface: Living apart from a partner is described as being like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is an example of what it defines: separately sits between to and live.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical construction where a word sits between to and its verb, as in to boldly go.

clue.text: Firm desire to return before Sunday — the rabbits!

parts.note: CO is company, a firm

indicators.note: come back, so the word for desire is read from the end to the start

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A company wanting to come back before the weekend ends, then rabbits appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Coney is an old word for a rabbit, still used in heraldry and for its fur.

clue.text: Urbane and married in comfort, mostly

indicators.note: the married letter goes within the soothing word
most of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to comfort is to soothe

explanation.surface: Sophisticated and wedded, mostly living in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SOOTHE to SOOTH, and 'in' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth describes suave, polished manners, much like urbane.

clue.text: Worry about show of hesitation for search

indicators.note: around, so the worrying word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: to worry is to fret
er is a hesitant sound in speech

explanation.surface: Fretting over a moment of doubt during a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret about is to rummage and hunt busily for something.

clue.text: Seek food seeing kid captured by the enemy

indicators.note: held prisoner inside, so the teasing word sits within the enemy

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
to kid is to tease, which is to rag

explanation.surface: Looking for something to eat after a child is taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but here it is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search for food, as animals do in the wild.

clue.text: The ruler lost time in anger, getting nothing right

indicators.note: taken away, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: temper means anger
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A monarch losing patience in a rage and gaining nothing by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes T from TEMPER, leaving EMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme ruler of an empire.

clue.text: One working on student is an animal

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming on a piece means following it

parts.note: L is the learner plate sign, a student
one is I, the Roman numeral
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone employed on a learner who turns out to be a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is a big cat, a large wild animal.

clue.text: Car that's at home in the road

indicators.note: the home word goes inside the road

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A car that feels comfortable on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a major British motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a classic small British car.

clue.text: Weapons are raised, to be comfortable

indicators.note: lifted up in a down clue, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: guns are weapons

explanation.surface: Raised firearms make for an easy feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means cosy, warm and comfortable.

clue.text: The ceremony in which company people welcome private soldiers

indicators.note: taking in a guest, so the company letters hold the soldiers inside

parts.note: CO is company
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A ceremony where an army company invites the troops in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private soldiers' is the crossword's usual OR, other ranks; 'welcome' tucks those soldiers into the company abbreviation, before the people word follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronation is the ceremony crowning a monarch.

clue.text: Fill in forms at election

indicators.note: sits within the words that follow, spanning their letters

explanation.surface: Filling in the ballot papers at polling time.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to satisfy fully, to fill to capacity.

clue.text: His drug den is shaky!

indicators.note: unsteady, so these letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: A dealer's hideout is on the verge of collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a drug den that is shaky is trembling.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuddering means trembling or quaking violently, a shaky state.
